PACKAGING NOTES / 02a few things to borrow and a few to leave out

Give them a reason to watch you

The title tells them what they'll learn. The thumbnail shows the work you're about to explain.

Do more of this

keep it easy to understand

Nathan Miller / published title

If your thinking about doing ecom in 2026 watch this... (brutally honest)

A board + a facecam

The board tells you what the video covers before you press play.

Borrow the simple recording setup. Give your own lesson a clear title.

Trading reference / published title

breakdown of the strategy that made me $124,550 last month

A specific result to explain

The title gives you a result and a timeframe. The normal speaking frame lets it carry the promise.

Show the trades behind that result inside the video. Explain what you did.

Avoid this framing

be specific about the lesson

TradingLab / published title

I Reveal My Most Profitable Trading Strategy

Hype takes up the space

"Insanely profitable" tells you very little about the lesson.

Name the setup or the problem it solves. Show a chart example you will actually explain.

TradingLab / published title

The Only Trading Strategy You'll Ever Need

The promise is too broad

"Only" and "ever" leave out who this is for and when it applies.

Use a specific case from your own work. Show what changed and why.

Use a result you can talk through

Pick the example first. Write the title around it, then use a frame from the chart, board or screen you'll explain.

YOUR TITLE EXAMPLE
my trading setup made me $139,200 last month...

Thumbnail: your chart and facecam. Open the video on the trades behind the result, then show how you took them.

The TradingLab examples have substantial reach. The notes here concern the promises and presentation. Views alone don't tell us whether viewers became buyers.
